title: Payback (remix EP)
label: Aftershock
format: EP (format not stated in sources opened)

type.basis: Coded for Terror Danjah's Frontline remix; several characters are drafted from descriptions of his style rather than this track.

sound.text: In FACT (2009) Simon Reynolds hears a 'harmonically rich', edge-of-dissonance synth on Terror Danjah's 'Creep Crawler' remix of 'Frontline'. Terror says it is a normal synth that he processes and textures, and won't say how.
Planet Mu (2009) describes Terror Danjah's general style: a signature palette of sounds he adds to occasionally, shifting syncopated rhythms around 140 bpm, and a gremlin-cackle audio logo.

context.text: Terror Danjah tells FACT (2009) that Payback, which followed the Industry Standard EP (2004), 'was the biggest' and one of Aftershock's top sellers; he singles out his 'Creep Crawler' remix of 'Frontline'.

The Aftershock (group) Wikipedia article lists Payback as a 2004 various-artist remix EP and repeats that it was one of the label's top sellers. It describes the original 'Frontline' (2003) as Big E-D featuring D Double E.
Terror Danjah (FACT, 2009): after Crazy Titch's 'I Can C U' and N.A.S.T.Y.'s 'Cock Back', Aftershock's third release was Big E.D.'s 'Frontline'.

uncertainty: No catalogue number, format or exact date was found. The Terror Danjah Wikipedia article says the 'Creepy Crawler' instrumental (2003) came out on Industry Standard (2004) and was voiced by Wiley as 'Take Chances', while FACT ties a 'Creepy Crawler' remix of Frontline to Payback. These may be the same riddim in two forms. The planet.mu sound description covers Terror's general style, not this record specifically.
tracklist: Full tracklist not found. FACT (2009) names the 'Creep[y] Crawler' remix of Big E-D's 'Frontline' as its standout. Planet Mu's Gremlinz (2009) opens with 'Big-E-D: Frontline (Terror Danjah's Creepy Crawler Remix)'.
